description: This topic provides a detailed overview of major lakes and waterfalls in India and across the world. It is a crucial segment of Static GK, highly optimized for rapid revision and competitive exam preparation.

sections.title: Types and Concepts of Lakes
sections.description: Basic concepts of different types of lakes and the geographical processes behind their formation.

key_concepts.explanation: A shallow body of water separated from a larger body of water (like an ocean) by barrier islands, sandbars, or coral reefs. Example: Chilika Lake.
A U-shaped body of water that forms when a wide meander of a river is cut off from the main channel, creating a free-standing lake. Example: Kanwar Lake.
A lake that forms in a volcanic crater, caldera, or in a depression caused by a meteorite impact. Example: Lonar Lake.

sections.title: Important Facts
sections.description: One-liner crucial facts related to lakes and waterfalls for direct exam questions.

important_facts.fact: Finland is widely known as the 'Land of a Thousand Lakes' due to the sheer abundance of lakes in its territory.
Cholamu Lake (Tso Lhamo), located in Sikkim, is the highest altitude lake in India.
The Dead Sea, situated on the border of Jordan and Israel, is the lowest lake and water body on the Earth's surface.
Lonar Lake in Maharashtra is a unique hyper-velocity meteorite crater lake; its water is both highly saline and alkaline.
